title: Semidefinite division with a nonnegative quotient
source_hypothesis: Smooth compact-time family with f(t0,y)=g(y), f and transverse differential zero on the central curve, weak sign agreement fg>=0 on an open neighborhood of the whole interval, and nonzero semidefinite transverse Hessian. The statement includes homogeneous principal-type tubes satisfying P.
reviewed_arguments: The sign condition is assumed on an open time neighborhood of the full compact interval. One exact parameter Morse square and common root-domain margins reduce the semidefinite case without changing time.

Smooth even/odd division gives an affine remainder. Both real roots force its coefficients to vanish on the negative parameter set; every boundary jet vanishes on its closure and the exact quotient is nonnegative there.

Uniform Taylor bounds for the remainder coefficients and displacement of the square variable by distance-to-closed-set to the Nth power prove that the negative quotient defect is smaller than every power of that distance.

A compact maximum gives a continuous flat bound. An explicit dyadic lattice covering has stated constants, bounded overlap and local finiteness. Normalized cutoff derivatives have every required distance estimate.

Local suprema and the partition give a nonnegative smooth majorant. All derivative bounds and the complete difference-quotient induction prove smooth extension with zero jets on an arbitrary closed set.

Adding that majorant corrects the quotient while preserving its exact prescribed values and the one-sided remainder support. Reversing signs and restoring degree-zero/degree-one homogeneity prove both semidefinite cases.
Together with the preceding indefinite proof this completes Proposition 26.5.7. The earlier semidefinite Hessian rank obstruction and the restricted indefinite affine claim remain unchanged.

Three complete solutions exhibit a negative preliminary quotient, its exact flat correction, a genuinely necessary remainder, and homogeneous positive and negative semidefinite characteristic realizations. X2 is a mathematical variant of the counterexample following Proposition 26.5.7, with a different flat exponential rate and a complete independent verification; X3 supplies its homogeneous realization.
